title: Semantic diversity beats photorealism in generated training sets
one_line_idea: Train classifiers on generated sets that deliberately trade photorealism for prompt-level semantic diversity and measure which axis buys more accuracy per sample.
problem: Practitioners select generated training images using realism-oriented metrics, implicitly assuming photorealism is the binding constraint on downstream utility.
core_hypothesis: At matched sample counts, generated sets optimized for semantic and layout diversity outperform sets optimized for photorealism on real-test accuracy, except in fine-grained texture-dependent regimes.
core_claim: At matched sample counts, generated sets optimized for semantic and layout diversity outperform sets optimized for photorealism on real-test accuracy, except in fine-grained texture-dependent regimes.
method_sketch: Using one text-to-image generator, build two matched-size training sets by steering sampling toward realism (guidance and quality filters) versus prompt diversity (attribute and context grids), train identical classifiers, and compare real-test accuracy on coarse and fine-grained tasks.
falsifiable_prediction: Diversity-steered sets beat realism-steered sets on coarse-grained real-test accuracy at matched size, and the ordering reverses on fine-grained texture-dependent classes.
why_important: Sampling and filtering budgets are finite; knowing which axis to buy changes the allocation in every synthetic-data pipeline.
why_possibly_novel: Realism-diversity trade-offs are discussed loosely, but a controlled single-generator factorial isolating the two axes at matched counts is not something I can point to as established; novelty unverified.

kill_risk: The two axes are hard to vary independently within one generator, so the manipulation may be confounded by sampler side effects.
community_default_belief: More photorealistic generated images are better training data because they are closer to the test distribution.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Classifiers may care more about covering label-relevant variation than about pixel-level realism, which augmentation practice suggests is often expendable.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: On one 10-class subset, train on a high-realism versus a high-diversity set of 5k images each; if realism wins on coarse classes too, the idea dies.

problem: Injecting synthetic data while a class is still improving on real data may interfere and certainly spends synthetic samples where they are not yet needed.

method_sketch: Implement online per-class loss plateau detection, inject class-conditional synthetic data on trigger, and compare final accuracy and synthetic-sample consumption against always-on mixing at matched real data.
falsifiable_prediction: Final accuracy is equal within noise while synthetic-sample consumption drops by a large factor, with per-class gains concentrated after each trigger.
why_important: It reduces generation costs and localizes in time when synthetic data actually contributes.
why_possibly_novel: Adaptive data injection exists in curriculum and active learning; per-class plateau triggers for synthetic injection seem new; novelty unverified.

why_it_might_be_wrong: Synthetic samples may be redundant while the real-data gradient signal for a class is still strong.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: A two-class pilot with manually chosen triggers; if late injection loses accuracy versus always-on mixing, kill.

problem: There is no accepted unit for comparing synthetic and real data quantities, so planning conversations lack a common currency.
core_hypothesis: Real-synthetic exchange rates measured at iso-performance are approximately invariant across training budgets within a task and transfer across tasks in the same domain with a systematic correction factor.
core_claim: Real-synthetic exchange rates measured at iso-performance are approximately invariant across training budgets within a task and transfer across tasks in the same domain with a systematic correction factor.
method_sketch: Measure iso-performance exchange rates between real and synthetic samples across training budgets and tasks, test within-task invariance, and identify covariates that break the invariance.
falsifiable_prediction: Within-task invariance holds within stated bands across budgets, while cross-task transfer requires a fitted task-difficulty correction.
why_important: Even a rough currency with error bars beats no currency for deciding between annotation and generation spending.
why_possibly_novel: Effective-number concepts exist for duplication and class imbalance; a validated exchange-rate calculus for synthetic-versus-real data seems unbuilt; novelty unverified.
novelty_hook: Effective-number concepts exist for duplication and class imbalance; a validated exchange-rate calculus for synthetic-versus-real data seems unbuilt; novelty unverified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Measure iso-performance exchange rates between real and synthetic samples across training budgets and tasks, test within-task invariance, and identify covariates that break the invariance.
main_risk: Exchange rates may vary so much with budget and regime that no useful invariance exists.
kill_risk: Exchange rates may vary so much with budget and regime that no useful invariance exists.
community_default_belief: Synthetic-data value is context-dependent and cannot be summarized in one number.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Scaling-law experience shows that rough summary quantities can work well enough to guide planning despite context dependence.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: Measure the exchange rate at two budgets in one task; large instability between them kills the currency idea.

title: Support coverage beats density matching for synthetic training value
one_line_idea: Disentangle whether the downstream utility of synthetic data tracks support coverage, touching all modes, or density matching, reproducing correct proportions.
problem: Synthesis pipelines aim to replicate the true distribution including its proportions, though training may only need the support covered.
core_hypothesis: At matched sample counts, coverage-optimized synthetic sets sampled near-uniformly over modes beat density-matched sets for downstream training, and density matching catches up only when explicit reweighting is added.
core_claim: At matched sample counts, coverage-optimized synthetic sets sampled near-uniformly over modes beat density-matched sets for downstream training, and density matching catches up only when explicit reweighting is added.
method_sketch: Sample from one generator under mode-uniform versus density-matched samplers estimated via clustering, train students on each at matched counts, and add an importance-weighted training arm to test the reweighting explanation.
falsifiable_prediction: The coverage-optimized set wins raw training, and the density-matched set closes the gap only with importance weighting.
why_important: It would redirect synthesis effort from matching proportions, which is hard, to covering support, which is easier and apparently what matters.
why_possibly_novel: Coverage-versus-density questions appear in generative evaluation; connecting them causally to downstream training value with sampler interventions seems fresh; novelty unverified.
novelty_hook: Coverage-versus-density questions appear in generative evaluation; connecting them causally to downstream training value with sampler interventions seems fresh; novelty unverified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Sample from one generator under mode-uniform versus density-matched samplers estimated via clustering, train students on each at matched counts, and add an importance-weighted training arm to test the reweighting explanation.
main_risk: Mode estimation via clustering is fragile, so the mode-uniform sampler may not implement the intended intervention.
kill_risk: Mode estimation via clustering is fragile, so the mode-uniform sampler may not implement the intended intervention.
community_default_belief: Synthetic data should replicate the true data distribution as closely as possible, proportions included.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Training can reweight proportions cheaply but cannot conjure missing modes.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: The two-sampler comparison on one dataset; density-matched winning kills it.

title: Prompt entropy as a ceiling predictor for synthetic-data gains
one_line_idea: Treat the entropy of the prompt or conditioning program as an information budget and test whether it predicts the ceiling of achievable downstream gains regardless of image count.
problem: Pipelines scale image counts indefinitely, though the images are samples from a distribution whose information content the conditioning program bounds.
core_hypothesis: For a fixed generator, downstream gains saturate at a level monotone in conditioning entropy, so richer prompt programs raise the ceiling even at matched image counts.
core_claim: For a fixed generator, downstream gains saturate at a level monotone in conditioning entropy, so richer prompt programs raise the ceiling even at matched image counts.
method_sketch: Construct prompt programs of graded entropy, generate matched-count pools per program, train students across increasing counts per program, and map gain ceilings against program entropy.
falsifiable_prediction: Low-entropy programs saturate early regardless of image count, and the ordering of gain ceilings follows the entropy ordering.
why_important: If conditioning entropy bounds gains, sampling budgets should be redirected toward conditioning design, inverting current practice.
why_possibly_novel: Information arguments about generated data circulate informally; an operational entropy-versus-ceiling measurement seems missing; novelty unverified.
novelty_hook: Information arguments about generated data circulate informally; an operational entropy-versus-ceiling measurement seems missing; novelty unverified.
minimal_falsification_experiment: Construct prompt programs of graded entropy, generate matched-count pools per program, train students across increasing counts per program, and map gain ceilings against program entropy.
main_risk: Prompt entropy is hard to define in a way that is comparable across program families, threatening the ordering claim.
kill_risk: Prompt entropy is hard to define in a way that is comparable across program families, threatening the ordering claim.
community_default_belief: Generating more images is the way to more gains; prompt variety is a secondary stylistic choice.
why_it_might_be_wrong: Sampling more from a fixed conditional distribution cannot exceed the information the conditioning carries, plus the generator prior.
fastest_falsifying_experiment: Two entropy levels crossed with two image counts; if low-entropy pools keep improving with count past the high-entropy trajectory, kill.
